milestone.title: raul TUI — make Settings a real lane (replace modal, add Save/Cancel)

intent.outcome: Settings becomes a 5th lane with its own flat-list render, Save/Cancel affordance, and unchanged Tab/Shift+Tab cycle semantics. The double-Esc-out-of-modal workflow disappears; the BF-05 Tab hijack disappears; editing still dry-runs through `mp config set` before each write.

problem.description: Today Settings opens as `Mode::Settings(SettingsState)` painted into `view.overlay_rect` (centered 70%×70% modal), with a centered popup layered on top for field editing. The BF-05 commit hijacks `Tab` and `BackTab` to `Action::JumpLane(0)` so they don't conflict with the field-edit buffer, which makes Tab from Settings go to Overview but Shift+Tab from Overview cannot reach Settings — the lane cycle is asymmetric. Esc has to be pressed once per layered overlay to escape (once for the popup, once for Settings), which is a real ergonomic cost. All of `crates/raul/src/tui/modes/settings.rs` (~219 lines), 8 Settings actions, the centered-popup overlay, and `tui_settings*`/`m168_settings*` tests exist only because Settings is a transient mode rather than a lane.

in_scope: Replace `Mode::Settings(SettingsState)` with a real lane: `Lane::Settings` already exists in `app.rs`'s `Lane::ordered()`; its render drops into the lane pane with the existing `Borders::ALL` chrome and the BF-03 grouped flat-list layout.

Add a footer-bar pair inside the Settings lane: `[Save (s)] [Cancel (Esc)]`. `s` writes the staged edits through `mp config set`, surfacing any dry-run / API failure in the footer flash; `Esc` discards them and stays on the lane (no lane change).

Drop the BF-05 Tab/BackTab hijack in `crates/raul/src/tui/modes/settings.rs:97-105`. Tab and Shift+Tab now use the default `next_lane` / `previous_lane` defaults — Settings is reached and left in both directions exactly like every other lane, with the default settings of Tab / Shift+Tab.

Remove `Mode::Settings(SettingsState)` and the 8 Settings-related actions: `OpenSettings`, `CloseSettings`, `SettingsEnter`, `SettingsSubmitEdit`, `SettingsBack`, `SettingsCancelEdit`, `PushInputChar`, `PopInputChar`. Replace with one new `Action::SettingsSave` carrying the staged-key writes.

Migrate `crates/raul/tests/tui_settings.rs`, `crates/raul/tests/tui_settings_automation.rs`, `crates/raul/tests/tui_settings_lane_smoke.rs`, `crates/raul/tests/m168_settings.rs`, `crates/raul/tests/m168_settings_grouped.rs`, `crates/raul/tests/m168_settings_hotkeys.rs`: keep the per-field dry-run + safety contract, port from modal-popup assertions to lane render assertions, drop the ones that asserted `Esc`-then-`Esc` semantics, and add a footer-bar assertion.

Replace the `SettingsState::new(config)` cache path with a lane-scoped ephemeral stage (App field or local variable): the lane reads the same `mp config show` payload, stages pending writes, and only commits them on `s`.

Update `crates/raul/src/tui/action.rs::apply_action`, `crates/raul/src/tui/runner.rs`, `crates/raul/src/tui/render/overlays.rs` to drop the Settings modal/overlay plumbing, and update `crates/raul/src/tui/keybinds.rs` to add an `open_settings` lane-activation default if needed (current `s` already works because `Lane::Settings` is already in the ordered list).

Update `crates/raul/src/tui/render/lane_lists.rs` (or wherever Settings ends up rendered) to surface the existing `SETTINGS_KEYS` enumeration under the new `[section]` group tags (BF-03) with the section header carrying the conventional `(total/visible)` count like other sections.

Update `docs/concepts/01 - Agent Integration/AGENT-READINESS.md` for the keybind change (`s` still opens, but now it's a lane transition rather than a modal; new `s` (save) reuses the same letter with different semantics — pick a different default or document the override).
Run `mp validate` after each plan write; keep dogfood-log entry inside this milestone's evidence.
out_of_scope: New keybinds. The existing `keybinds.open_settings` (default `s`) and `keybinds.escape` (default Esc) keep their role; this milestone does not introduce a new top-level keybind.
New config keys. Everything writes through the existing schema; no `ui.settings.*` plumbing lands here.
Mouse/wheel handlers. Reuse the lane-list mouse path that exists for Milestones/Backlog.
Section-iconography changes (BF-03 introduced `◆` for the section header and `[section]` tags).

Persisting the staged edits across launches. Each launch loads from `mp config show` and stages fresh — if the user closes the TUI without `s`, the unsaved edits are lost. The agent-automation commit-after-execute path is unchanged.
Cross-platform / accessibility work — the footer-bar save/cancel pair is keyboard-driven exactly as the rest of raul.

Restoring the `BackTab → Settings` loop while keeping the BF-05 hijack anywhere — the hijack goes away. If someone wants a quick jump back to Settings later, the override lives on `next_lane` like every other default.
Touching M167's chrome findings (lane tab bar, M167 chrome pass) — they already landed clean and remain valid.

acceptance_criteria.description: Pressing Tab while the active lane is Settings, Milestones, Backlog, Overview, or Path cycles app.active_lane along Lane::ordered() (wrapping at end). Pressing Shift+Tab cycles the same set in reverse. There is no BF-05 hijack: the literal Tab key inside Settings no longer reaches Action::JumpLane(0), and Shift+Tab from Overview reaches Settings rather than stalling.

design_decisions.choice: Replace the centered modal with a 5th lane rendering the existing SETTINGS_KEYS flat list inside the lane pane.
design_decisions.rationale: Removes the layered Esc escape, removes the BF-05 Tab hijack, and unifies Settings with the lane cache, footer, header, and chrome — keeping Settings as a special case is what created the asymmetry. The lane already exists in Lane::ordered(); only the rendering plumbing needs to switch.

design_decisions.choice: Footer-bar pair [Save (s)] [Cancel (Esc)] plus an Action::SettingsSave for the save keymap.
design_decisions.rationale: A footer affordance survives keymap changes, mirrors Milestone/Backlog footer hints, and makes Esc the only cancel path so we don't introduce a new keybind. s was previously open_settings; we keep it for save and document the override because rebinding open_settings would chase a different chord elsewhere.

design_decisions.choice: Replace the centered field-edit popup with an inline buffer rendered as a second row of the same group section (or as an ephemeral overlay on the lane). No permanent modal state; the buffer dies the moment the lane is left.
design_decisions.rationale: Aligns with the edit-and-commit-after-execute model that the agent-automation block already proves out: staging stays in-memory, s flushes each stage through mp config set --dry-run then commits the whole batch, and leaving the lane (Esc → cancel / Tab + Shift+Tab → next lane) discards pending edits by construction.

design_decisions.choice: Drop BF-05 entirely; Tab and Shift+Tab cycle both ways through Settings exactly like every other lane.
design_decisions.rationale: BF-05 was a punt on the field-edit popup's keyboard collision. Once Settings is a lane with an inline edit buffer (or any buffered input stays inside one field at a time), the tab conflict disappears and the hijack is no longer load-bearing. The user's keyboard contract becomes uniform.

design_decisions.choice: Keep the existing per-field mp config set --dry-run check. SettingsSave runs dry-run across every staged edit before commit; any failure aborts the batch and surfaces the API error in the footer flash. No new commits reach disk on a partial failure.
design_decisions.rationale: Matches the BF-04 dry-run contract used by tui_settings_automation; the test fixture already exists.

design_decisions.choice: Settings remains a single pane with the existing flat-list rendering; no group flattening (BF-03), no icon reworking, no new section vocabulary.
design_decisions.rationale: BF-03 grouped settings with [section] tags (ui / workflow / git / next / agent / keybinds) and per-group section counts; that work is shipping-ready and the lane simply reuses it.

open_questions.question: Should s (the existing default open_settings) be rebound to settings_save and open_settings move to a new chord (e.g. Ctrl-S or :settings)?
open_questions.answer: s stays as the save key. open_settings gets a new default chord Ctrl-O; the existing single-binding default s is re-bound via config.toml. Document both in AGENT-READINESS.

open_questions.question: Tab keymap during an active inline edit buffer — should Tab still complete the edit (commit) instead of cycling lanes, mirroring modal-era semantics?
open_questions.answer: Inside the Settings lane, Tab commits the active edit if there is a staged value (or moves to the next field when no edit is active); Tab cycles lanes only when no edit is active and no field is focused. Shift+Tab is the symmetric inverse.

verification.evidence: M169-rev: four findings from external review remediated in place. (1) HIGH: load_settings_lane early-returns when app.settings is populated; JumpLane(4) / mouse-click of Settings tab while already on Settings no longer wipes staged_edits. (2) MED: set_config_value removed; apply_settings_commit_edit no longer shadows mp's parse_bool/parse_icons coercion; apply_settings_enter prefers staged_edits over mp config get for re-edit buffer. (3) MED: apply_settings_save now tracks committed keys on commit-time failure and surfaces partial state via reload_settings_after_save_keeping - failed key stays in staged_edits, committed keys are dropped so retry only re-tries the failed one. (4) LOW: tab_move_up/down now wrap (AC-01 verbatim). (5) LOW: staged_edits is BTreeMap<String,String> for deterministic key-sorted iteration. 14 regression tests in crates/raul/tests/m169_rev.rs; 2342/2342 tests pass; clippy + fmt + doctor + dep-audit-raul + mp validate + mp milestone verify all green.
